title: When AI's Thirst Trumps Human Needs: Tahoe's Power Shift
caption:
Lake Tahoe residents are losing power. Not due to a storm, but because their energy supplier chose to prioritize data centers. It’s a stark signal of AI’s growing infrastructure demands and the real-world trade-offs emerging. 

Get the critical context on AI's energy footprint. Tap "BUILD" for our field guide.

slides.headline: Lake Tahoe residents abandoned for AI's energy *appetite*.
slides.sub: How data centers are pushing communities offline.

slides.title: The Unseen Power Grab
slides.body: An energy supplier in Lake Tahoe diverted power from local homes to serve data centers. This isn't a fluke; it's a stark example of how AI's insatiable demand for electricity is reshaping infrastructure priorities.

slides.definition: The practice where high-demand tech industries (like AI data centers) consume disproportionate energy resources, often at the expense of local communities' stability and access.
slides.example: Residents faced blackouts as power was rerouted to a growing cluster of AI data centers.

stats.label: Projected global electricity consumption by data centers by 2030.

audiences.body: Facing blackouts, higher utility costs, and a diminishing sense of priority in their own communities.
Caught between growing demand from AI giants and the need to maintain reliable service for existing customers.
Indirectly benefiting from cheap, consistent power, often without direct engagement with the social costs.

slides.title: Beyond Tahoe: A *Precedent* Set
bullets: This isn't an isolated incident; similar tensions are emerging globally.
AI's infrastructure demands will force difficult conversations about resource allocation.
Expect more regulations and public scrutiny as energy conflicts escalate.
slides.footer: The era of cheap, abundant energy for AI is ending. Fast.
